title: Howard Hughes' 30,000-acre Las Vegas land buy for $3 an acre eventually became Summerlin
summary_full: In 1952, Howard Hughes embarked on a visionary project by purchasing 30,000 acres of barren land in Las Vegas, aiming for development. It wasn't until 1988 that plans for Summerlin came to life, culminating in construction that began in 1990, highlighting its residential beginnings. Today, Summerlin has blossomed into a vibrant community spanning 22,500 acres, hosting over 130,000 residents along with schools, parks, and commercial areas, showcasing its rich identity.
